comment: Known behavioral and option-surface gaps per utility, each a short sentence naming the option or behavior. Lanes update their own utilities.

fmt: Uutils adds -m/--preserve-headers and -T/--tab-width, which GNU 9.12 fmt does not provide; its generated -h and -V forms are also absent from GNU.
id: Uutils adds --ignore, -A, -p, and -P; XSH supports the -a no-op but not its --ignore alias, and also omits the generated -h and -V forms.
kill: Uutils adds -L as an alias for -t/--table and generates -h and -V; XSH exposes the table option only as -t/--table and omits the generated short help/version forms.
mkdir: Uutils adds generated -h/-V; XSH accepts -Z/--context as GNU does without SELinux (silent, or a warning for a value).
mkfifo: Uutils adds generated -h/-V; XSH accepts -Z/--context as GNU does without SELinux (silent, or a warning for a value).
mknod: Uutils adds generated -h/-V; XSH accepts -Z/--context as GNU does without SELinux (silent, or a warning for a value).
mktemp: The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; XSH accepts only the long help/version forms.
shuf: Uutils adds --random-seed, which XSH explicitly rejects as a uutils extension and directs callers to --random-source=FILE; the generated -h and -V forms are also absent.
shred: The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; XSH accepts only the long help/version forms.
cat: XSH retains GNU's hidden ---presume-input-pipe test option, which uutils cat does not expose; uutils also generates -h/-V while GNU 9.12 cat omits both short controls.
cut: The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; XSH accepts only the long help/version forms.

df: Pinned uutils permits zero or more values for --output, while XSH accepts one optional value; uutils also generates -V, which XSH omits.
echo: Uutils generates -h and -V help/version controls; XSH follows GNU echo's manual scan for -n, -e, and -E, so those short controls are printed as text.

hostid: The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; GNU 9.12 hostid has no matching short forms, so XSH accepts --help and --version without them.

basename: Text applets still require UTF-8 arguments; the launcher now supports raw argv only for scripts declaring List[Bytes] rest arguments.
The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; GNU 9.12 basename's short-option string omits both, so XSH accepts --help and --version without them.
whoami: The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; GNU 9.12 whoami has no matching short forms, so XSH accepts --help and --version without them.
ls: SELinux contexts (-Z, --context), ACL/context mode markers and capability colors remain incomplete despite the shared xattr API.
Names sort bytewise (the C locale); a UTF-8 locale's `strcoll` order (test_ls_sort_dot_first_utf8_locale, the UTF-8 branch of test_ls_order_time_breaks_ties_by_name) is not implemented.
Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset (`EST5`, `<+03>-3`); zone names and DST rules need a tz database (`%Z` shows the TZ abbreviation as written).
Terminal width comes from COLUMNS or 80: there is no TIOCGWINSZ query, so a terminal's real width is not used.
Non-UTF-8 operands cannot be passed (xsh rejects non-UTF-8 argv); non-UTF-8 entry names are quoted from their raw bytes but sorted and matched by their lossy text.
Directories are read eagerly: /proc/self/fd can expose a directory descriptor after it closes. unix.window_size exists but terminal-width selection still needs parity verification.
stty: Integer arguments follow the uutils tests' overflow wording (`Value too large for defined data type`); GNU 9.4 on the host prints `Numerical result out of range`. One constant (`OVERFLOW_TEXT`) in core/stty.xsh flips it if the 9.12 source says otherwise.
Fractional speeds (`9600.49`) are accepted as the uutils tests require; GNU 9.4 on the host rejects them as `invalid ispeed`.
Arguments after `--` are settings; GNU 9.4 silently ignores them.

A terminal that keeps other state than requested (a pty drops parity and sizes other than 8 bits) is reported as `unable to perform all requested operations`; GNU 9.4 reports `Invalid argument` for some of those from tcsetattr itself, which `unix.set_tty_attrs` does not raise.
`-g` prints 32 control characters like glibc, but the kernel keeps 19: a saved state that sets later ones is applied and then refused as GNU does.
more: Single-key paging, Ctrl-C handling and resize redraws remain missing; unix.read_fd and unix.poll_fd now provide the required descriptor operations.
A pipe on standard input is printed in full instead of paged; command input from /dev/tty is not integrated.
Non-UTF-8 operands cannot be passed (this text applet requires UTF-8 argv): test_more::test_more_non_utf8_paths.

test_more::test_invalid_file_perms needs a non-root user and the lowercase `permission denied` of Rust's ErrorKind; the applet prints strerror text (`Permission denied`) and root can read the file anyway.
-u strips underline and bold overstrikes; there is no terminfo standout mode to switch to otherwise.
The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; XSH accepts only the long help/version forms.
mv: Uutils adds -g and generated -h/-V; XSH accepts -Z/--context as GNU does and shares the backup and update options with pinned uutils.
pr: Zero-valued `--width`, `--columns`, `--length`, and `--page-width` diagnostics use GNU's xstrtol wording; pinned uutils tests expect clap wording. For `--pages=0`, GNU reports `invalid page range '0'` while uutils expects `invalid --pages argument '0'`.

Pinned uutils requires a value for -e/--expand-tabs; XSH accepts it optionally. XSH also exposes -i/--output-tabs, -c/--show-control-chars, and -v/--show-nonprinting, which pinned uutils omits; uutils generates -V, which XSH omits.
rm: Pinned uutils has a hidden test switch --presume-input-tty and its ---presume-input-tty alias; XSH omits both along with uutils-generated -h and -V.
who: Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset (`EST5`, `<+03>-3`); zone names and DST rules need a tz database, and an unset TZ reads as UTC instead of /etc/localtime (request: a local-time primitive).

`who -b` and the boot record synthesized for a default utmp file without one derive the boot time from `unix.uptime_seconds` (whole seconds), so it can differ from GNU's by a second at a minute boundary.
`--lookup` canonicalizes nothing: `dns` has no canonical name (getaddrinfo AI_CANONNAME), so numeric hosts pass and a host name fails with an explicit message (request: `dns.canonical`).

test_who::test_too_many_args and the two test_who::*_piped_to_dev_full tests assert clap and uutils wording; the applet prints GNU 9.4's `extra operand 'u'` and `who: write error: No space left on device`.
The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; XSH accepts only the long help/version forms.
users: Sessions of the default utmp file are checked for live pids (`process.kill` with signal 0) as gnulib does; an explicit FILE is listed as written.
The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; XSH accepts only the long help/version forms.
uptime: Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset; an unset TZ reads as UTC instead of /etc/localtime (request: a local-time primitive).
`-p` and `-s` are procps options (not GNU coreutils); they are implemented because the uutils tests exercise them.
test_uptime::test_uptime_with_extra_argument asserts clap wording (`unexpected value 'b'`); the applet prints GNU's `extra operand 'b'`.
The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; XSH accepts only the long help/version forms.
pinky: Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset; an unset TZ reads as UTC instead of /etc/localtime (request: a local-time primitive).

Accounts come from /etc/passwd (`lib.auth`, or XSH_PASSWD_FILE) rather than NSS, and `user.lookup` has no GECOS field (request: `gecos` on `user.lookup`). XSH_UTMP_FILE replaces /var/run/utmp for tests.
`--lookup` canonicalizes nothing: `dns` has no canonical name (getaddrinfo AI_CANONNAME), so numeric hosts pass and a host name fails with an explicit message (request: `dns.canonical`).

stdbuf: Child libc buffering cannot be controlled by parent pipes or XSH byte streams. GNU/uutils stdbuf requires an ABI-compatible preload shared library with a setvbuf constructor; the standalone static musl release ships no such library. The applet validates options and exits 125 explicitly without launching a command.
The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; XSH accepts only the long help/version forms.
timeout: --foreground is explicitly rejected: managed spawn owns a new process group and transfers terminal ownership; leader-only signaling cannot provide the foreground process contract without a native spawn policy. Durations currently round positive intervals to a millisecond because time.millis is the narrowest public constructor.
The pinned uutils Clap builder generates -h and -V as short help/version controls; XSH accepts only the long help/version forms.
awk: Parser and interpreter are implemented in XSH; full GNU awk language, locale and regex parity remains unverified.
sed: Parser and execution are implemented in XSH; GNU extensions and multibyte locale parity remain incomplete.
mkfs.fat: Regular image files only; full device and dosfstools option parity remains incomplete.
fsck.fat: Regular images only; primary BPB recovery, active-FAT selection, root expansion and dot-entry repair remain incomplete.
getfacl: POSIXLY_CORRECT and terminal indentation parity remain incomplete.
setfacl: Conditional X uses original mode; recursive traversal aborts on a child failure. Validated sequential writes can retain earlier changes after a later syscall failure.
setcap: Force coercion is unsupported; stdin EOF and blank-line behavior still differ.
dig: A/AAAA over UDP only; full resolver, TCP fallback and dig option parity remain incomplete.
nslookup: A/AAAA over UDP only; full interactive and resolver behavior remains incomplete.
getent: XSH account parsing is implemented; complete NSS database parity remains incomplete.
login: Authentication policy is XSH; full PAM, session accounting and controlling-terminal parity remains incomplete.
dmesg: Metadata, follow, clear and console controls are unsupported.
sysctl: Key reads and writes are implemented; enumeration remains incomplete.
hwclock: RTC drift, device selection and local-time modes remain incomplete.
flock: Descriptor operands, unlock and timeout modes remain incomplete.
switch_root: Additional command argv and full root-transition fidelity remain incomplete.
reboot: Direct syscall requires explicit --force; service-manager shutdown is unsupported.
poweroff: Direct syscall requires explicit --force; service-manager shutdown is unsupported.
halt: Direct syscall requires explicit --force; service-manager shutdown is unsupported.

tee: Uutils adds -i/--ignore-interrupts and generated -V; XSH omits these forms.
touch: Uutils generates -V as a short version control; XSH accepts only --version. The obsolete -f/--force no-op is parsed but unused on both sides.
sort: Uutils adds --help, --key, --output, --field-separator, --parallel, --compress-program, --random-source and random-sort controls; XSH exposes key/output/separator only as short forms and omits the other options. Uutils also accepts repeated -c/--check values, while XSH limits --check to one optional type and keeps -c as a flag.
